### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | *(see summary — defaults to publisher-level policy unless a journal-specific override was found)* |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | conditional |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 |
| **Summary** | Journal-specific AI policy page for Death Studies (tandfonline udst20 Instructions for Authors) returned 403/redirect errors and could not be directly confirmed; facts below are from Taylor & Francis's publisher-wide AI Policy, which the publisher states individual journals may narrow further. Generative AI must not be listed as author (no authorship, no accountability capacity). Permitted uses: idea generation/exploration, copyediting/language improvement/translation, LLM-enhanced literature search, literature classification, coding assistance -- all require author review for accuracy. Disclosure required: submissions must include a statement naming the tool (with version), how it was used, and why. Prohibited: text/code generation without rigorous revision, synthetic data generation to substitute missing data, AI-generated/manipulated research-data images (figures, clinical samples, diagnostic images); these may trigger editorial investigation. Peer reviewers/editors are barred from uploading unpublished manuscripts into generative AI tools. |
| **Source URL** | https://taylorandfrancis.com/our-policies/ai-policy/ |

### Preprint Policy

> AI-research note (not broken down per-stage): Yes -- Taylor & Francis's general supportive preprint stance applies to Death Studies: authors may post to non-commercial preprint servers (e.g. arXiv, bioRxiv, SocArXiv) before/during submission without it counting as duplicate publication, and may share the Author's Original Manuscript freely via preprint servers, scholarly networks, social media, or personal websites.
> Source: https://authorservices.taylorandfrancis.com/publishing-your-research/making-your-submission/posting-to-preprint-server/

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** Journal actively covers: qualitative/phenomenological grief and bereavement studies (interview-based, cross-cultural), quantitative and psychometric studies on prolonged grief disorder (incl. ICD-11 PGD diagnostic criteria work), suicide/suicidal-ideation studies (survey, cohort, police-record, social-media-data), cross-national and cross-cultural comparative studies, network-analysis methodology (e.g. cross-lagged panel network models), mixed-methods and arts/humanities approaches to mourning (photography, tattoos, children's drawings), historical/anthropological/sociological perspectives on death, and book reviews. Recent (2025-2026) special issues confirm continued interest in death education/pedagogy, the social-political life of the dead, materiality of death/mourning cross-culturally, and 'meaning in mourning.' No currently-open call-for-papers was found on the special-issues page as of 2026-07-13 -- the four most recent special issues (2025-2026) have already published; no upcoming/open CFP listed.

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** qualitative/phenomenological interview studies, cross-sectional survey and cohort studies, psychometric/scale-validation studies, cross-lagged panel network analysis, cross-national/cross-cultural comparative studies, mixed-methods studies, historical/anthropological/sociological analysis, book reviews

**Fields deliberately left blank, and why:**
- **ai_policy.gate / journal-specific confirmation**: Death Studies' own tandfonline 'Instructions for Authors' page (udst20) returned HTTP 403 / unrelated redirects on repeated fetch and browser-navigation attempts; could not confirm whether the journal narrows the publisher-wide AI policy (T&F states some journals restrict AI use beyond language-improvement only). Reported facts are the publisher-wide policy, flagged as such.
- **experiential.desk_reject_pct**: SciRev shows 'n/a' for immediate-rejection percentage (editor has not supplied it), and no forum/cross-language source (muchong, zhihu, fabiaoji sites, Reddit) discussed desk-reject rates for this journal specifically.
- **experiential.reviewer_culture**: No concrete first-hand source (SciRev free-text comments are limited to one motivation blurb about a qualitative paper being accepted faster than expected; no discussion of reviewer tone/culture) and cross-language search (muchong, zhihu, Reddit AskAcademia) returned zero relevant threads, so no subjective reviewer-culture claim can be sourced.
